what: Several stacked layers (like back, middle and front cities) each rise by their own distance over the same scroll length, starting the moment the plate’s top edge touches the top of the screen. Each layer follows at twice the page’s speed and stops at a different time (default 600, 1200 and 860px), so front layers cover back layers as they fill in, creating depth. The distance is proportional to the 1440 design width, min(width × px/1440, px), tied directly to scroll with no curve

options.rise: Distance each layer rises (px, space- or comma-separated in layer order), default 600 1200 860 — if there are more layers, the last value repeats
options.rise-sp: Distance to use below 767px, same as the default rise · Site 600 800 590
options.width: Design width (px), default 1440 — on narrower screens the distances shrink by the same ratio
options.[data-fx-part=layer]: Layers to raise (one or more). Stack them inside the panel with position and set front-to-back order with z-index
options.width-sp: Design width (px) below 767px, same as the default width · 390 (the original --design-width is 390 on phones)
